insight.obstacle: To refute a universal graph inequality, constructing a large graph alone is insufficient; its clique-minor parameter and chromatic number must be separated by a strict, quantified bound.
insight.strategy: Decompose the counterexample into (1) an existence construction for arbitrarily large finite graphs with independence number at most two and a small connected-matching number, (2) a general matching–minor inequality bounding the Hadwiger number by vertex count and connected-matching number, (3) a graph-coloring lower bound from independence number, and (4) a short rational-inequality chain that makes the two bounds strictly separate. Keep the expensive object-existence argument independent from the small generic inequality bridge so later constructions can reuse or replace either layer.
